title: Deterministic reachability validator against movement.json
summary: The validator every generated route must pass: a deterministic reachability search that accepts a route segment only if each transition is achievable under config/movement.json with a 15% margin (85% of max reach and distance) AND its entry prerequisites (min speed, plant window) and surface prerequisites (wall-run min wall length, grapple anchor reach) are met. Also enforces beat 1 = T0 set and the rule that a tool may be required to summit only if it is taught in an earlier beat (never beat 1). Shared movement contract with the controller.

acceptance_tests.test: Given a traversal graph and a proposed route, the validator returns valid/invalid per segment, using only config/movement.json constants at an 85% margin and checking each transition's entry + surface prerequisites; identical input yields identical output.

Property tests cover unreachable summit, a gap just over 85% of max distance (rejected) and just under (accepted), the beat-1 verb restriction, an unmet tool prerequisite (rejected), and a route that requires a tool not introduced in an earlier beat (rejected).
The validator loads the shared constants via services/traversal/movement.py (M0-MOVE-01); no movement number is duplicated.
Reviewed by gj-gameplay so the validator and the controller agree on the constants.

history.event: sharpened under AUTH #023 (journey generation v1): validator also checks entry + surface prerequisites and enforces the tool-taught-before-required rule; property tests extended to unmet tool prerequisites and tools required without an earlier teaching beat.

Builder (AUTH #027, gj-scenegraph hat): built services/traversal/reach.py — the deterministic reachability validator. check_transition re-derives each edge's margin from config/movement.json via the shared affordance library (AT-3: no movement number duplicated; loaded through services/traversal/movement.py) and rejects anything over the 0.85 margin or whose verb cannot apply. validate_route returns per-segment valid/invalid (AT-1) and enforces the route rules: segments chain end-to-end, beat 1 is T0-only, and a tool may be required only if an earlier beat (never beat 1) taught it. Property tests (AT-2): gap just under 85% accepted / just over rejected, tier mismatch rejected, inapplicable verb rejected, unreachable summit, beat-1 T0 restriction, unmet tool prerequisite, tool used before taught, broken chain, and determinism. 39 green across the service; ruff + format clean. AT-4 (gj-gameplay/controller agree on constants) is satisfied by construction — the validator and the Unity controller both read config/movement.json through the same loader + the M0-MOVE-01 C#/Python agreement fixture — and is offered for gj-gameplay's independent look. AT-1..AT-4 met. open → done.
